Connectivity hooks::useOffline.summary: Reads whether the app is currently offline. This experimental hook is available in Client Components when experimental.useOffline is enabled.
Connectivity hooks::useOffline.explanation: Call useOffline in a Client Component to read Next.js's connectivity state. With experimental.useOffline enabled, it reports offline conditions from browser events or failed supported requests; Next.js changes it back when connectivity is restored. Without the configuration flag, it always returns false.
Connectivity hooks::useOffline.returns: boolean: true when the app is offline; false when it is online or rendering on the server.

example.explanation: This Client Component displays the current connectivity state.

useCases.scenario: Show a banner or status label when connectivity is lost.

useCases.title: Offline-aware loading UI
useCases.scenario: Provide an offline-specific Suspense fallback while dynamic content waits.

useCases.title: Retry status
useCases.scenario: Indicate that a navigation, prefetch, or Server Action is waiting to retry.

keyPoints: The hook gives a boolean offline indicator.
Use the result for banners, status indicators, or other connectivity-aware UI.
The hook has no arguments.
Its return type is boolean.
A true result means the app is considered offline.
A false result means online or server rendering, and is also the initial hydrated value.
When the connection returns, supported blocked requests are retried automatically.
gotchas: The hook is experimental and should not be relied on as a production-stable API.
If experimental.useOffline is not enabled, the hook always reports false.
During server rendering and before hydration finishes, false is expected even if the device is offline.

Connectivity hooks::useOffline and hydra.summary: useOffline returns whether a Next.js App Router application is offline. Its initial false value during server rendering and hydration makes connectivity UI a progressive enhancement.
Connectivity hooks::useOffline and hydra.explanation: Enable the experimental configuration option to activate connectivity tracking and retries, then call useOffline in a Client Component. The hook returns false while rendering on the server and during initial hydration, so the browser’s first reliable value arrives after mounting; this conservative start supports hydration-safe progressive enhancement.
Connectivity hooks::useOffline and hydra.returns: boolean: true when the app is offline; false when online, rendering on the server, or before hydration completes.

example.explanation: A Client Component changes its fallback message when the browser reports an offline state.

useCases.scenario: Show a banner when the browser loses connectivity.

useCases.title: Loading feedback
useCases.scenario: Provide an offline-aware Suspense fallback while dynamic content waits.

useCases.title: Pending requests
useCases.scenario: Explain that a soft navigation or Server Action is waiting for reconnection.

keyPoints: useOffline reports the application’s current offline state as a boolean.
The hook is available only with the experimental configuration enabled; otherwise it remains false.
Call the hook without arguments.
The initial false value is conservative and should be treated as progressive enhancement for hydration safety.
After connectivity returns, blocked navigation or content requests can retry and continue automatically.
Use the post-mount value for connectivity-specific UI rather than relying on the server-rendered result.
gotchas: The feature is experimental and may change, so avoid depending on it in production without accepting that risk.
Do not assume the first returned value reflects the browser’s actual connectivity; it is false until hydration progresses.
Offline handling applies to supported soft navigations and requests, not an offline full-page reload.

Hook patterns::Active links from usePath.summary: Use usePathname in a small Client Component to compare the current pathname with each link's href. Import that component into a shared layout so only the navigation depends on the URL.
Hook patterns::Active links from usePath.explanation: Put the pathname-dependent navigation in a small Client Component and render that component from the shared layout. usePathname updates after client-side navigation, letting each link compare its href with the current path without making the entire layout request-dependent.
Hook patterns::Active links from usePath.returns: The usePathname hook returns the current URL pathname as a string.

To change them, serialize the current value into a new URLSearchParams object, modify that copy, and use useRouter or Link to navigate to the updated URL.

Hook patterns::useServerInsertedHTML.summary: useServerInsertedHTML lets a CSS-in-JS registry place collected styles into server-rendered HTML. A Client Component wraps the app, extracts styles in the callback, flushes the registry, and returns the styles for insertion before dependent content.

Navigation hooks::useRouter.summary: `useRouter` enables imperative navigation from Next.js App Router Client Components. Its router object can push or replace routes, refresh data, prefetch routes, and traverse browser history.
Navigation hooks::useRouter.explanation: Import `useRouter` from `next/navigation` inside a Client Component to obtain an imperative router object. Use its methods for client-side navigation, history traversal, prefetching, or refreshing the current route; use the separate pathname, search-parameter, and dynamic-parameter hooks for URL data.

parameters.description: Destination route, typically an internal path.

parameters.name: options

Navigation hooks::useRouter.returns: A router object exposing `push`, `replace`, `refresh`, `prefetch`, `back`, and `forward` methods.

keyPoints: It provides imperative route changes from client-side React code.
`router.push(href, options)` navigates without a full page reload and adds a browser-history entry.
`router.replace(href, options)` navigates while replacing the current history entry.
`router.refresh()` requests the current route again and updates server-rendered output.
`router.back()` moves backward through browser history.
`router.forward()` moves forward through browser history.
`router.prefetch(href)` loads route data ahead of navigation to improve responsiveness.

Do not import the App Router hook from `next/router`.

Navigation hooks::useRouter back and for.explanation: In an App Router Client Component, call useRouter from next/navigation to obtain the router object. router.back() moves to the previous entry in the browser history, while router.forward() moves to the next entry, avoiding a newly supplied destination URL.

Pass only a trusted internal path to push or replace; never forward raw user-controlled URL text, because a value such as a javascript: URL can execute in the page context and create an XSS vulnerability.

Observability hooks::useReportWebVitals.summary: useReportWebVitals invokes a callback with available Web Vitals metrics so a Client Component can forward them to an analytics endpoint. Keep the callback reference stable to avoid duplicate reports.
Observability hooks::useReportWebVitals.explanation: Place the hook in a Client Component and pass it a stable callback. Next.js invokes the callback with metric data as it becomes available, allowing the complete object to be forwarded to an endpoint for real-user performance tracking.

Rules and boundaries::Hooks in Client Co.summary: Navigation and browser hooks such as useRouter, usePathname, and useSearchParams must run in Client Components. Place "use client" at the top of the module that uses them, creating the Server–Client boundary.
Rules and boundaries::Hooks in Client Co.explanation: In the App Router, navigation hooks belong in Client Components rather than Server Components. Put "use client" before imports in the module that uses them; its imported module graph becomes client-side, while a Server Component can render that client component and pass serializable data to it.

parameters.name: href, options
parameters.description: `href` is the destination route; `options` may configure scrolling and transition types for navigation methods such as `router.push`.

Rules and boundaries::Hooks in Client Co.returns: useRouter returns a router object with methods including push, replace, refresh, prefetch, back, and forward; usePathname returns the current pathname; useSearchParams returns the current URL search parameters.

Rules and boundaries::Next.js hook migra.sourceTitle: How to migrate from Pages to the App Router
Rules and boundaries::Next.js hook migra.summary: When moving a screen into the App Router, replace next/router with navigation hooks from next/navigation. Use separate hooks for navigation, pathname, search parameters, and dynamic route parameters.
Rules and boundaries::Next.js hook migra.explanation: When a screen moves into the app directory, replace next/router usage with hooks from next/navigation. Use useRouter for programmatic navigation, usePathname for the current pathname, useSearchParams for query-string values, and useParams for dynamic route parameters. These hooks are Client Component APIs, so add the client directive and do not call them from Server Components.

parameters.description: No parameters are documented for useRouter, usePathname, or useSearchParams.

URL hooks::useParams.summary: `useParams` is a Client Component hook for reading dynamic parameters from the active URL. It returns the matched segments as an object, with strings for ordinary segments and string arrays for catch-all segments.
URL hooks::useParams.explanation: Import `useParams` from `next/navigation` inside a Client Component. It returns the active route's dynamic segments as an object: a single segment is a string, while catch-all segments are arrays of strings. Routes without dynamic segments produce an empty object.
URL hooks::useParams.returns: An object containing the current route's filled dynamic parameters. Each key is an active dynamic segment; each value is a string or an array of strings based on the segment type. With no dynamic parameters, it returns an empty object.
